model_system: FGFR2-TACC fusion CCA patient-derived xenograft (CTG-0997, FGFR2-TRA2B fusion) plus a panel of FGFR1/2/3-altered cell-line xenografts
control_arm: vehicle; cisplatin alone in the combination arm
dose_and_schedule: 0.3 or 1 mg/kg PO once daily x 42 days
mechanism: Selective ATP-competitive inhibitor of FGFR1/2/3 (IC50 0.4/0.5/1.0 nM, sparing FGFR4 at 30 nM). In an FGFR2-fusion tumor the fusion drives ligand-independent FGFR signaling, and the drug shuts that down.
key_finding: In the FGFR2-fusion CCA PDX, 10 of 12 tumors shrank at 1 mg/kg and both doses beat vehicle on growth inhibition (P<0.01). Adding cisplatin outperformed either agent alone.
caveats: The CCA PDX carries an FGFR2-TRA2B fusion rather than the more common FGFR2-BICC1; the patient's fusion is untested (ngs_pending).

model_system: Patient-derived FGFR2-G3BP2 fusion intrahepatic CCA matched cell line, organoid, and xenograft (DUC18828)
dose_and_schedule: pemigatinib 3 mg/kg PO + quisinostat 16 mg/kg PO, 5 days/week
mechanism: A high-throughput screen of >2,100 compounds across the matched models flagged HDAC inhibition as the strongest partner for FGFR blockade. The combination cut proliferation and pushed cells into apoptosis beyond what FGFR inhibition managed alone.
key_finding: The pemigatinib-quisinostat pair shrank PDX tumors by 59.4% versus 23.8% for pemigatinib alone and 15.1% for quisinostat alone, with matching gains in the organoid and cell line. This is one of the few preclinical platforms built from a fusion-positive intrahepatic CCA patient.
caveats: Single-patient model with an FGFR2-G3BP2 fusion; the HDAC combination is investigational, not the on-label monotherapy the patient would receive first.

model_system: Patient-derived FGFR2-fusion intrahepatic CCA cells with acquired kinase-domain resistance mutations; serial biopsies and ctDNA from 4 patients pretreated with BGJ398 or Debio 1347
dose_and_schedule: in-vitro potency profiling against FGFR2 kinase-domain mutants; clinical dosing in the paired patients
mechanism: Irreversible covalent pan-FGFR inhibitor binding outside the ATP cleft, so several FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations that block reversible inhibitors (e.g. V564F, N550H) stay sensitive.
key_finding: TAS-120 held activity against multiple FGFR2 resistance mutations that emerged on BGJ398 or Debio 1347, and the four patients who progressed on those reversible inhibitors responded to TAS-120. The mutation that resisted TAS-120 differed from the ones resisting reversible drugs, which points to a sequencing strategy.
caveats: Mechanism-of-resistance study in fusion-positive intrahepatic CCA, so it matters only after FGFR2 confirmation and prior FGFR-inhibitor exposure. Heavy reliance on ctDNA and a small patient set.

model_system: Alb-Cre Kras-G12D IDH1-R132C/H genetically engineered mouse model of intrahepatic CCA; syngeneic allografts from IDH1-R132C tumor lines, with NSG immunodeficient controls
control_arm: vehicle; same cell lines in immunodeficient NSG mice
dose_and_schedule: AG-120 (ivosidenib) oral dosing in syngeneic and NSG hosts
mechanism: Mutant IDH1 generates R-2-hydroxyglutarate, which blocks TET2 and the cell's interferon-gamma response, letting the tumor hide from immune attack. Inhibiting mutant IDH1 reactivates TET2, switches on viral-mimicry transposable elements and cGAS-STING, and restores IFN-gamma sensitivity.
key_finding: AG-120 dropped R-2HG by more than 85%, slowed syngeneic tumors, and extended survival, but did nothing in immunodeficient NSG mice carrying the same cells, so the antitumor effect runs through the immune system. The drug also synergized with CTLA-4 blockade, clearing tumors in most treated animals.
caveats: Mouse genetics pair IDH1-R132 with Kras-G12D, which is not the typical human IDH1-mutant CCA background; the immune-dependent mechanism may overstate single-agent benefit seen clinically in ClarIDHy.

model_system: HER2-amplified gastric models: NCI-N87 cell-line xenograft and GXA 3054 patient-derived xenograft
dose_and_schedule: 4-30 mg/kg IV; NCI-N87 at 4 mg/kg, GXA 3054 PDX at 30 mg/kg
mechanism: Biparatopic antibody binding the ECD2 (pertuzumab) and ECD4 (trastuzumab) epitopes on adjacent HER2 molecules, which forces HER2 into large surface clusters. The clustering drives receptor internalization, blocks ligand-dependent and independent signaling, and uniquely triggers complement-dependent cytotoxicity alongside ADCC and ADCP.
key_finding: Zanidatamab outperformed both trastuzumab and the trastuzumab-pertuzumab pair, with 268% growth-rate inhibition at 4 mg/kg in NCI-N87 (versus 86% and 155%) and tumor regression in the high-HER2 PDX. The CDC arm is unique to zanidatamab and absent from the comparators.
caveats: Efficacy shown in gastric models, not biliary; HER2 biology is shared but no CCA xenograft tested here. Mouse complement is impaired, so the CDC contribution measured in human serum may not carry into the in-vivo models.

model_system: Admixed HER2-high (3+) and HER2-negative tumor-cell xenografts modeling HER2 heterogeneity; NCI-N87 and HER2-variable lines
dose_and_schedule: single IV dose in xenograft bystander experiments
mechanism: HER2 antibody linked to a membrane-permeable topoisomerase I inhibitor (DXd) at a drug-to-antibody ratio of 8. After internalization and cathepsin cleavage, the payload diffuses out and kills neighboring cells regardless of their own HER2 level.
key_finding: DS-8201a killed HER2-negative cells when they were mixed with HER2-positive cells, an effect T-DM1 did not produce. This bystander killing explains activity across heterogeneous and lower-HER2 tumors, which fits the variable HER2 staining seen in biliary tract cancer.
caveats: Bystander mechanism shown in breast/gastric-type models, not biliary; relevance to CCA rests on the IHC-driven DESTINY-PanTumor02 signal rather than a CCA xenograft.

model_system: BRAF V600E A375P melanoma and Colo205 colorectal xenografts; rat skin model for paradoxical lesions
dose_and_schedule: dabrafenib 30 mg/kg PO + trametinib 0.3 mg/kg PO daily, up to 90 days
mechanism: Dabrafenib blocks mutant BRAF and trametinib blocks MEK downstream, so the combination hits two nodes of the MAPK cascade. Doubling up suppresses the MEK-driven pathway reactivation that lets tumors escape single-agent BRAF inhibition.
key_finding: The combination beat either drug alone for tumor growth control in both V600E xenografts and prevented the hyperproliferative skin lesions that single-agent BRAF inhibition caused in rats. That dual benefit, efficacy plus less paradoxical toxicity, is the rationale for combining the two clinically.
caveats: Melanoma and colorectal models, no biliary tissue; BRAF V600E signaling is shared but CCA-specific preclinical data are sparse. Supports the tumor-agnostic mechanism behind the ROAR biliary cohort.

model_system: KM12 colorectal cells carrying a TPM3-NTRK1 fusion; subcutaneous KM12 xenografts and a patient-derived sarcoma model
dose_and_schedule: 60 or 200 mg/kg/dose PO daily x 14 days
mechanism: Selective TRK inhibitor (IC50 3.5 nM against TPM3-TRKA in KM12) that shuts down fusion-driven TRK autophosphorylation and the downstream AKT and ERK signaling the fusion turns on.
key_finding: Larotrectinib stopped KM12 xenograft growth and dropped pTRK, pAKT, and pERK, with activity holding across TPM3-NTRK1, MPRIP-NTRK1, TRIM24-NTRK2, and ETV6-NTRK3 variants. The matched patient with an NTRK fusion sarcoma responded.
caveats: Colorectal and sarcoma models, not biliary; the case rests on the tumor-agnostic fusion mechanism since NTRK fusions are under 1% in CCA.

model_system: CCDC6-RET non-small-cell lung and RET-C634W medullary thyroid cell-line xenografts plus two CCDC6-RET patient-derived xenografts
mechanism: Highly selective ATP-competitive RET inhibitor (wild-type IC50 0.92 nM, >250-fold selective over most other kinases) that blocks fusion-driven and mutant RET signaling, including the V804 gatekeeper variants.
key_finding: Selpercatinib gave dose-dependent tumor growth inhibition exceeding 90% and drove complete regressions in several RET fusion or mutant models at 3-10 mg/kg. Selectivity against non-RET kinases predicts the clean off-target profile seen clinically.
caveats: Lung and thyroid RET models, no biliary tissue; relevance to CCA is the tumor-agnostic RET-fusion mechanism, and RET fusions are rare in biliary tract cancer.

model_system: Panel of KRAS G12C cell-line and patient-derived xenografts (NSCLC, colorectal, pancreatic); biliary not represented
n_units: broad model panel, per-arm n not reported
dose_and_schedule: oral dosing across the xenograft panel at well-tolerated levels
mechanism: Covalent inhibitor (IC50 ~5 nM) that locks the mutant cysteine-12 of GDP-bound KRAS G12C, holding the protein inactive and cutting off downstream RAS signaling.
key_finding: Adagrasib produced broad antitumor activity across KRAS G12C models, with complete responses in a subset, at tolerated doses. The work also mapped co-mutations and feedback reactivation that shape which tumors respond.
caveats: No biliary model in the panel; KRAS G12C is roughly 1% of CCA, so this is mechanism support for a rare candidate feature rather than a tissue-matched proof of concept.

exclusion_reason: The predictive axis here is host neoantigen load from mismatch-repair deficiency or high TMB, not a tumor-cell drug target that preclinical mouse or organoid work can model for this patient. The mechanism evidence for anti-PD-1 in dMMR tumors is human (Le et al.) rather than a CCA-specific preclinical proof of concept, so it backs the biomarker but adds nothing to a targetable-feature preclinical dossier.

Entrectinib preclinical work covers the same TRK-fusion mechanism in colorectal (KM12) and neuroblastoma models already captured by the larotrectinib row, with no biliary tissue. For the NTRK candidate feature it duplicates rather than extends the included TRK proof of concept.
